title: analytics: /analytics/query ignores record-level scoping — a member counts and reads dimension values of records they cannot read
body:
Found while verifying the 17.0.0-rc.1 checklist on #3909 (section C, "Analytics: RLS/tenant scope on ObjectQL path #3597"). Verified on `main` @ `1ee48bc60`, showcase under `os serve --dev`, two real signed-in principals.

**`POST /api/v1/analytics/query` does not apply record-level scoping. A caller can count — and, via `dimensions`, read the field VALUES of — records the data API correctly refuses them.**

## Repro

`showcase_private_note` is `sharingModel: 'private'`. Admin owns 5 notes; a plain member holds shares on exactly 2 of them and no `viewAllRecords` anywhere.

The data path is correct:

```
GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note   as admin  → total 5
GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note   as member → total 2     ✅ OWD + shares
```

The analytics path is not:

```
POST /api/v1/analytics/query {"cube":"showcase_private_note","measures":["count"]}
  as admin  → [{"count":5}]
  as member → [{"count":5}]      ❌ counts 3 records it may not read
```

And it is not limited to counts — grouping discloses the values themselves:

```
POST /api/v1/analytics/query
     {"cube":"showcase_private_note","measures":["count"],"dimensions":["title"]}
  as member →
    [{"title":"rc1 rule target","count":1},   ← entitled
     {"title":"rc1 secret","count":1},        ← entitled
     {"title":"rls-probe-1","count":1},       ← NOT entitled
     {"title":"rls-probe-2","count":1},       ← NOT entitled
     {"title":"rls-probe-3","count":1}]       ← NOT entitled

GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note?select=title   as member
  → ["rc1 secret","rc1 rule target"]          the same caller, the same field
```

So any authenticated user who can reach `/analytics` can enumerate the field values of every row of any object exposed as a cube, regardless of OWD, sharing rules, or RLS. `title` here is innocuous by construction; the same query shape against a real deployment's objects reads whatever the grouping column holds.

**Method note (this cost me a false negative first):** a permission set carrying `viewAllRecords` had been bound to my member during an earlier export test, which made the two paths agree at 5/5 and look correct. The divergence only appears once the caller genuinely lacks VAMA. Anyone re-testing should confirm the data path returns FEWER rows than the admin before reading anything into the analytics numbers.

## Scope check

`/analytics` mounts only when the capability exists (#4019 — verified separately, holds), the entry validates its body (#4010 — holds), and a measure emits its declared aggregate (#4184 — holds). The scoping layer is the piece that is absent: the SQL the endpoint returns in `data.sql` carries only the caller's own `WHERE` (e.g. the `dateRange` predicate from #3650), never an owner/share/RLS predicate.

## Expected

The analytics path resolves through the same execution context as `/data`, so the compiled query carries the caller's read filter (owner scope + share grants + RLS), and a dimension can only group by values inside that scope. Fail-closed if the scope cannot be resolved, matching the posture #3989 took for the empty-slot case.

Part of the #3909 rc.0/rc.1 verification (section C).
